steps.intent: France's primary objective is to renew the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts for twelve months to safeguard the 2015 Algiers Peace Agreement and maintain independent reporting on the ground, especially in the context of MINUSMA's ongoing withdrawal. We anticipate strong resistance from the Russian Federation, which, aligning with the Malian junta's demands, is pushing to dismantle the Panel of Experts and terminate the sanctions regime entirely. Preserving the integrity of the Panel of Experts' independent monitoring while averting a Russian veto will be the central challenge of the negotiations.

messages.Albania: Albania fully supports the draft resolution prepared by France and co-sponsored by the UAE to renew the 2374 sanctions regime and extend the mandate of the Panel of Experts. Given the precarious security situation and MINUSMA's ongoing withdrawal, preserving the sanctions regime and the independent reporting of the Panel of Experts is essential to deter spoilers and support the 2015 Algiers Peace Agreement. We stand ready to vote in favour of the text as drafted.
messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the draft resolution renewing the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts pursuant to resolution 2374 (2017). We believe the sanctions regime remains an important tool to support the 2015 Agreement on Peace and Reconciliation in Mali emanating from the Algiers process, which is essential for lasting peace. We encourage the penholders and Council members to maintain constructive dialogue with the Malian transitional authorities and regional partners to ensure unity and effective cooperation on the ground.
messages.China: China has always maintained that sanctions are a means rather than an end, and should not be maintained indefinitely. Given the evolving reality on the ground and the withdrawal of MINUSMA, the Security Council must give full consideration to the legitimate concerns and views of the Malian Government. We urge the penholders to conduct further consultations to accommodate the concerns of all parties and avoid forcing through a text that lacks consensus.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador fully supports the draft resolution renewing the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts on Mali. In light of the ongoing drawdown of MINUSMA, these mechanisms remain vital tools to deter spoilers, monitor the situation on the ground, and support the implementation of the 2015 Agreement on Peace and Reconciliation. We thank France and the United Arab Emirates for their leadership and are ready to support the text as drafted.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports the renewal of the sanctions regime to uphold the Algiers Peace Agreement, which remains essential for stability in Mali. However, sanctions should never be punitive or perceived as undermining national sovereignty, especially in the context of MINUSMA's ongoing drawdown. It is vital that the Council takes into account the concerns of the Malian transitional authorities and fosters constructive engagement rather than confrontation.
messages.Ghana: Ghana expresses its full support for the renewal of the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts established pursuant to resolution 2374 (2017), which remain vital tools for supporting the implementation of the 2015 Algiers Agreement and deterring spoilers of peace. We believe our proposed minor adjustments will reinforce the crucial role of regional organizations such as the African Union and ECOWAS, while promoting a constructive, cooperative working relationship between the Panel of Experts and the transitional authorities of Mali. We commend the co-penholders for their constructive draft and look forward to its prompt adoption.
messages.Japan: Japan fully supports the draft resolution circulated by France and the United Arab Emirates to renew the Mali sanctions regime and extend the mandate of the Panel of Experts for another year. Especially in light of MINUSMA's ongoing drawdown and withdrawal, the 2374 sanctions regime and the independent monitoring provided by the Panel of Experts remain indispensable tools for deterring spoilers and supporting the implementation of the 2015 Agreement on Peace and Reconciliation. We appreciate the co-penholders' balanced text and hope the Council can demonstrate unity in adopting it without delay.
messages.Malta: Malta expresses its full support for the draft resolution circulated by France and the United Arab Emirates to renew the Mali sanctions regime and extend the mandate of the Panel of Experts. In light of MINUSMA's ongoing drawdown, preserving this targeted framework and the independent monitoring of the Panel of Experts is indispensable for supporting the 2015 Algiers Peace Agreement and protecting civilians. We stand ready to support the adoption of this text as drafted.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique supports the extension of the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, which remain critical tools for supporting the implementation of the 2015 Algiers Peace Agreement and preserving stability in Mali. In light of current political and security dynamics, it is essential that the Panel of Experts works collaboratively and constructively with the transitional authorities of Mali. We commend the co-sponsors for their efforts and encourage reaching a broad consensus within the Council.
messages.Russian Federation: The draft circulated by the penholder completely ignores the position of the sovereign authorities of Mali and fails to reflect the evolving reality on the ground following the termination of MINUSMA's mandate. Russia will not accept the extension of the mandate of the Panel of Experts, whose reporting has become entirely politicized and detrimental to the peace process, nor an indefinite sanctions regime. Our position is clear and non-negotiable: we can only support a final 12-month extension of the sanctions measures with a clear sunset clause, along with the immediate dissolution of the Panel of Experts.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland fully supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, which are indispensable tools for monitoring the 2015 Peace Agreement and promoting stability, especially amid MINUSMA's drawdown. We propose reflecting the standard application of resolution 2664 (2022) and strengthening language on international humanitarian law and the protection of civilians. We stand ready to work constructively with the co-penholders to secure adoption.
messages.United Arab Emirates: As a co-sponsor of this draft resolution, the United Arab Emirates fully supports the text as drafted to renew the sanctions regime and extend the mandate of the Panel of Experts. The targeted measures established under resolution 2374 (2017) remain a crucial instrument to support the 2015 Algiers Peace Agreement and foster stability in Mali. We encourage all Council members to support this balanced draft and stand ready to work with all delegations to preserve Council unity.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports the draft resolution circulated by France and the United Arab Emirates. With MINUSMA's drawdown underway and the 2015 Algiers Agreement under acute pressure, maintaining the 2374 sanctions regime and preserving the independent monitoring work of the Panel of Experts are essential to deter spoilers and track threats to peace and security. We commend the penholders' leadership and stand ready to vote in favour of the text as drafted.
messages.United States of America: The United States strongly supports the draft resolution circulated by France and the United Arab Emirates to renew the Mali sanctions regime and extend the mandate of the Panel of Experts. Especially in light of MINUSMA's ongoing drawdown, maintaining these targeted measures and the Panel's independent reporting is critical to preserving the Algiers Agreement and holding accountable those who threaten peace and stability. We appreciate the penholder's efforts and stand ready to vote in favor of this text as drafted.

steps.summary: France, as penholder alongside the UAE, has accommodated constructive proposals from the A3, Switzerland, and China by incorporating references to regional organizations, Mali's sovereignty, international humanitarian law, and potential reviews of the measures. However, France firmly rejects the Russian Federation's demand to terminate the Panel of Experts and impose a terminal sunset clause, which would destroy the Council's ability to deter spoilers and independently monitor violations in Mali, especially following MINUSMA's departure.

before.France:
France, together with the United Arab Emirates as co-penholder, has submitted this draft resolution to renew the targeted sanctions regime established pursuant to resolution 2374 (2017) and the mandate of the Panel of Experts for one year. 

At a critical juncture marked by the ongoing withdrawal of MINUSMA, the sanctions regime remains an indispensable instrument to preserve the 2015 Agreement on Peace and Reconciliation in Mali, deter violations of the ceasefire, and support efforts toward stability and the protection of civilians. The text before us reflects extensive consultations, incorporates balanced compromises, and takes into account the perspectives of the Malian transitional authorities, including the establishment of benchmarks to guide the future of these measures. We urge all members of the Security Council to vote in favour of this draft resolution to reaffirm our collective commitment to peace in Mali and the wider Sahel region.
before.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation cannot support the draft resolution submitted by France and the United Arab Emirates.

Throughout the negotiation process, our delegation consistently advocated for a realistic and balanced approach that takes into account the fundamental changes on the ground in Mali, following Bamako's sovereign decision regarding MINUSMA, as well as the position of the Malian authorities. The sanctions regime established pursuant to resolution 2374 (2017) was originally adopted at the request of the Government of Mali to support the implementation of the Algiers Agreement. Today, that regime has become outdated and counterproductive, and the Panel of Experts has increasingly transformed into an instrument of political pressure in the hands of external actors.

We proposed a pragmatic compromise: to extend the targeted measures for a final twelve-month period with a view to their complete termination, while immediately dissolving the Panel of Experts, whose activities no longer correspond to the reality on the ground and hinder the stabilization efforts of the host government. Unfortunately, the sponsors chose to ignore our clear red lines and the legitimate interests of Mali, presenting a text that maintains business as usual.

Under these circumstances, Russia will vote against the draft resolution.
before.United Arab Emirates:
The United Arab Emirates, as co-penholder alongside France, has engaged constructively throughout the negotiations on this draft resolution with the aim of achieving a balanced text that reflects the Security Council's continued commitment to peace, stability, and security in Mali. 

The targeted sanctions regime established pursuant to resolution 2374 (2017) remains a crucial mechanism to support the implementation of the 2015 Agreement on Peace and Reconciliation in Mali, which is vital for the country's long-term stability. The draft resolution before us today carefully takes into account the developments on the ground and emphasizes the primary responsibility and sovereignty of Mali, while providing for dialogue and review mechanisms. We urge all members of the Council to vote in favour of this text to maintain the Council's support for the Malian people and regional peace efforts.

after.China:
China’s position on the issue of sanctions has always been consistent. We have always maintained that sanctions are a means, not an end. The Security Council should approach sanctions with prudence and caution, ensure that sanctions measures are targeted, and avoid their indefinite application.

The targeted sanctions regime on Mali was established in 2017 at the request of the Malian Government to support the implementation of the Agreement on Peace and Reconciliation in Mali. In reviewing the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, the Security Council should fully respect Mali’s sovereignty, listen carefully to the views and legitimate concerns of the Malian Government, and maintain close communication with the country concerned.

China notes that the co-penholders made efforts during the consultations. However, the draft resolution just voted on failed to fully accommodate the core concerns of the country concerned and did not bridge the major differences among Council members, leading to division within the Council. China consistently advocates that Council members should seek the broadest possible consensus through patient consultations and avoid forcing a vote when sharp differences remain. Based on this consistent position, China abstained in the voting on the draft resolution.

At present, the situation in Mali is at a critical juncture. The international community should keep in mind the overarching goal of peace and stability in Mali and the wider Sahel region, fully respect Mali's ownership, and provide constructive support to help Mali tackle security challenges, fight terrorism, and improve people's livelihoods. China stands ready to work with the international community to continue playing a constructive role in achieving lasting peace, stability, and development in Mali.
after.France:
France deeply regrets the Russian Federation’s veto of the draft resolution submitted jointly with the United Arab Emirates. Thirteen members of this Council voted in favour of the text, demonstrating broad, cross-regional unity and support for the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts.

Throughout the negotiations, our delegation, alongside the United Arab Emirates, worked tirelessly and transparently to find compromises, accommodating the views of all Council members as well as taking into account the perspectives of the Malian transitional authorities, including by introducing language on clear benchmarks to review the measures. 

By casting its veto, Russia has chosen to isolate itself and act against the collective will of this Council. It has single-handedly dismantled a mechanism established in 2017 to support the Agreement on Peace and Reconciliation in Mali emanating from the Algiers process, at a critical and precarious time when MINUSMA is withdrawing and tensions are escalating on the ground.

The Russian Federation's real motives are no secret to anyone: this veto is a blatant attempt to silence the Panel of Experts and prevent independent reporting on violations of human rights, international humanitarian law, and the destabilizing activities carried out in Mali by mercenaries of the Wagner Group.

France remains steadfastly committed to the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of Mali, as well as to the Malian people. We will continue to support the full implementation of the Algiers Agreement and all efforts aimed at achieving lasting peace and stability in Mali and the wider Sahel.
after.Switzerland:
Switzerland voted in favour of the draft resolution presented by the co-penholders, France and the United Arab Emirates, and we thank them for their tireless efforts to reach a balanced compromise. We deeply regret the use of the veto by the Russian Federation, which has prevented the Council from renewing the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts.

The targeted sanctions regime established under resolution 2374 (2017) and the Panel of Experts were created to support the implementation of the 2015 Agreement on Peace and Reconciliation in Mali emanating from the Algiers process. At a particularly fragile moment, marked by the ongoing withdrawal of MINUSMA and escalating tensions on the ground, the preservation of this framework was more necessary than ever. The Panel of Experts provided the Council with objective, impartial, and independent information, which is indispensable for assessing the situation, including compliance with international humanitarian law and human rights law.

The draft resolution took into account the developments on the ground and the concerns expressed by Mali, notably by introducing clear benchmarks with a view to reviewing the measures. It received the overwhelming support of thirteen members of this Council. Paralyzing this instrument does a disservice to the peace process and leaves the Council with fewer tools to monitor and deter actions that undermine peace, security, and stability in Mali.

Switzerland reiterates its call on all signatory parties to uphold their commitments under the 2015 Agreement, to respect the ceasefire, and to resume dialogue. Above all, we remain steadfast in our commitment to the Malian people, who continue to bear the brunt of insecurity, and we urge all parties to strictly respect international humanitarian law and ensure the protection of civilians.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom voted in favour of the draft resolution co-sponsored by France and the United Arab Emirates, and we deeply regret that Russia chose to cast a veto against it.

Thirteen members of this Council voted in support of a balanced, carefully negotiated text that would have extended the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts for another year. At a critical time when MINUSMA is withdrawing and the security situation in Mali is deteriorating, the sanctions regime remains an indispensable tool to support the 2015 Agreement on Peace and Reconciliation and deter those who seek to undermine it.

Russia’s veto is reckless and deeply irresponsible. It undermines the Council’s efforts to support peace and stability in Mali and the wider Sahel. But Russia’s motivations are transparent to all: this veto was cast to shield the Wagner Group from scrutiny. The Panel of Experts has provided independent, objective reporting on the destabilizing presence and activities of Wagner personnel in Mali, including severe human rights abuses and violations. Russia has once again demonstrated that it will prioritize its own narrow, self-serving interests and those of its mercenaries over the peace, security, and well-being of the Malian people.

The United Kingdom remains steadfast in its support for the 2015 Peace Agreement and will continue to work with regional and international partners to promote peace, accountability, and stability in Mali and across the Sahel.
after.United States of America:
I thank the co-penholders, France and the United Arab Emirates, for their tireless efforts to craft a balanced text that garnered the support of 13 members of this Council.

The United States voted in favour of this draft resolution because the targeted sanctions regime established under resolution 2374 (2017) and the independent reporting of the Panel of Experts remain vital tools to support the 2015 Agreement on Peace and Reconciliation in Mali, deter violations of the ceasefire, and hold accountable those who obstruct the peace process and commit atrocities.

We deeply regret that the Russian Federation chose to use its veto today to terminate the mandate of the Panel of Experts and dismantle this critical mechanism. Russia’s action is not about supporting the Malian people, nor is it about respecting sovereignty. Russia used its veto to advance its own narrow, self-serving interests and to silence the independent, objective reporting of the Panel of Experts—reporting that has documented the destabilizing presence, human rights abuses, and predatory activities of the Kremlin-backed Wagner Group in Mali.

At a time when MINUSMA is withdrawing from Mali under difficult circumstances, the need for independent monitoring and Council oversight is greater than ever. By vetoing this resolution, Russia has once again undermined the Council’s ability to promote peace and security, abandoning the signatories to the Algiers Agreement and leaving the Malian people more vulnerable to further violence and instability.

Despite Russia’s obstruction, the United States remains firmly committed to supporting the people of Mali, promoting accountability, and working with regional and international partners to achieve lasting peace and stability.
